articleTitle: Sponsor Presentation: Mobile WiMAX Signals: What They Look Like Without The Maths
abstract: Many people coming to WiMAX are familiar with either WLAN or cellular formats. Mobile WiMAX signals conceptually combine elements of both types of signals, but with many novel aspects. The 5ms frame timing is similar to GSM, as is the use of a Base Station derived "rubber clock" in the mobile. The use of multiple orthogonal sub-carriers is familiar from WLAN, as are some aspects of the MIMO operation. What's new is a kind of symbol by symbol frequency hopping to provide frequency diversity, and the introduction of "collaborative" MIMO to help spectrum efficiency in the Uplink. This short presentation uses pictures instead of maths to bring out what the resultant signals look like. It also shows how key measurements can be quickly and effectively made on what are some of the most complex radio signals we've yet encountered.

articleTitle: Maximising the ROI for Deploying Mobile WiMAX Networks
Mobile WiMAX Strategy: Development and Deployment
abstract: There are two major technology and social trends significantly changing peoples' lives: Wireless and the internet. Leveraging these two trends, WiMAX creates a new utility enabling new services development and new Internet business model. Sprint Nextel has completed a through technology comparison and business case study, and selected WiMAX as the technology to make the "Internet everywhere" vision reality. Our goal is to reach 100 million POPs coverage by end of 2008, and we intend to expand Mobile WiMAX network coverage thereafter.

articleTitle: Deploying Mesh and WiMAX to Deliver Broadband Applications
abstract: Discussing the roles of broadband wireless technologies (WiFi, Mesh, WiMAX) in delivering robust scalable networks to satisfy the increasing demand for mobile media, internet access, surveillance and communications. In the context of actual examples, this discussion will focus on the complimentary advantages of each technology, how they are used together and how each benefit from the others.

articleTitle: The use of Fixed Broadband Infrastructure for vehicle location and traffic management
abstract: This paper outlines the details on ongoing technology trials carried out by XCD Communication Ltd on behalf of Transport for London. The purpose of the trial was to investigate the possible combination of GPS based vehicle location technology and Fixed Wireless Access communications in relation to their potential use in Road User Charging or Distance Based Charging. The trial examined the key wireless performance characteristics, a possible system architecture as well as the definition of a business use case. The paper outlines the advantages of adoptioning WiMax as a preferred wireless access technology.

articleTitle: The Need for WiMAX picocell & Femtocells
abstract: A collection of slides from the authorpsilas conference presentation is given. The following topics are covered: WiMAX picocell and femtocells; WiMAX basestations; indoor coverage; and 3G communication.

articleTitle: Comparing Mobile and Fixed WiMAX for Broadband Wireless Access
abstract: The presentation comprises a collection of slides. It discusses the comparison in both technicalities and user experiences of mobile and fixed WiMAX for broadband wireless access.

articleTitle: Broadband Wireless Access: Technical Challenges, Standards and Technologies
abstract: The article consists of a Powerpoint presentation on broadband wireless access. The areas discussed include: broadband wireless access and evolution of requirements from fixed to mobile services; the BWA channel; WiMaX Forum and IEEE 802.16 specifications; transmission and multiple access technologies: OFDM, single-carrier transmission (SCT) and OFDMA; multiple antenna (MIMO) options and tradeoffs; link adaptation.

articleTitle: Imperatives for the Wireless Internet & Mobile WiMAX Devices
abstract: This paper presents a collection of slides. It explains how innovation in the Internet and demand for mobility will drive the wireless Internet. Bandwidth, cost structure/integration and device proliferation will drive WiMAX adoption. WiMAX is the promise of the mobile wireless Internet.

articleTitle: Wireless systems deployment to provide public safety in Russia
abstract: A collection of slides from the author's conference presentation is given. This paper presents wireless technologies for safety systems.

articleTitle: Intended Applications and Real Life Experiences with Deployments of Aperto's PacketMAX
abstract: The article consists of a Powerpoint presentation on intended applications and real life experiences with deployments of Aperto's PacketMAX. The areas discussed include: WiMax system; VoIP; QoS; etc. etc. ldquo listing some of the slide titles.

articleTitle: Demonstrating the Benefits of the Multi Antenna Signal Processing features of WiMAX: A Case Study
abstract: This article consists of power point presentation on ArrayComm multiple antenna signal processing for WiMAX. It demonstrably confirmed the benefits of A-MAS, delivers substantial performance improvements, easy to integrate into a WiMAX BS architecture, Wave#2 compliant flexible solution and improves performance for all zones. Hardware-in-Loop is a valuable demonstration tool for realistic, demonstrative and versatile real performance measurement. It easily measure and investigate DSP implementation issues.

articleTitle: Realising the WiMAX Opportunity in the Middle East
abstract: This paper describes the technical and business planning that is required for an effective commercial WiMAX deployment. It is based on our experience of winning the licence to build and operate a national WiMAX network in the Kingdom of Bahrain. Although specific to WiMAX technology, the major part of the work described here was not technical; the small size of Bahrain made the radio planning requirements relatively straightforward. Instead, the focus is on the development of the network operator's business plan through the modelling of demand and the definition of marketable services that can be supported over the WiMAX based infrastructure In addition to specific observations from our experience n Bahrain, we also discuss the more general opportunities for WiMAX as a technical option for building sustainable business
